newsitem.title: USA: Stocks end mixed, Dow edges up to another record.
newsitem.headline: Stocks end mixed, Dow edges up to another record.

text.p: Stocks turned in a mixed performance Monday, with the Dow Jones industrial average eking out another record while high-technology stocks fell ahead of several key reports on the economy.
The 30-share Dow rose 7.67 points to 8,121.11, edging past the previous record of 8,116.93, set Thursday. It was the Dow's fourth record in the past five sessions.
In the broader market, advancing issues beat decliners, 1,440 to 1,415, on moderate volume of 464 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index, heavily weighted with tech stocks, fell 6.05 points to 1,563.53.
Investors will get the first of several economic reports Tuesday, with the release of the second-quarter employment cost index, which is watched closely as a harbinger of possible inflation.
Stocks that are especially sensitive to swings in the economy fared best Monday, a sign portfolio managers were adjusting their holdings in anticipation of strong economic data, analysts said.

"The consensus is the reports will show stronger economic growth than had been thought but not enough to cause interest rate concerns," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Kemper Funds. "So now you're even seeing the cyclicals have their run."
As a group, economically sensitive "cyclical" stocks have underperformed the broader market amid worries that a move by the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates would slow economic growth.
Those concerns faded last week when Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's comments to Congress were generally interpreted to mean the Fed was leaning against an imminent move on rates.
Other reports due later this week include the first estimate of the gross domestic product for the second quarter and the monthly jobs report for July, due Thursday and Friday.

Among the strongest Dow stocks were the cyclical issues Aluminum Co. of America, up 2 to 86-5/16; Sears, Roebuck and Co., which rose 7/8 to 62-11/16; and General Motors Corp., which rose 1-3/4 to 58-5/8. GM also gained from quick resolutions to strikes at plants in Ontario and Michigan.
Notably absent from the rally were tech stocks, which ended generally lower.
"There are some real value worries in the techs, especially if you look at the computer makers," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany.

Such concerns prompted one analyst, Andrew Neff at Bear Stearns, to cut his rating on Dell Computer Corp. to accumulate from buy. Shares in Dell fell 2-5/8 to 78-7/8 in the first trading session after its 2-for-1 stock split.
The selling spread through the personal computer group, pulling Compaq Computer Corp., down 3-1/8 to 132-1/2 and International Business Machines Corp., down 2 to 105.

Among individual issues, Donna Karan International Inc. climbed 1-3/8 to 11-13/16 after the company named long-time Polo Ralph Lauren Corp. executive John Idol as its new chief executive, charging him with restoring the company to profitability.
The American Stock Exchange index added 1.55 points to 639.35.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 8,867.934, off 17.770, or 0.2 percent.
